rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help — a concrete starting point". It read: "Hi Priya, Thanks for this, and good to hear you liked the meetup talk. Here's something concrete and bounded that would genuinely help. I've settled on a narrow focus for Halcyon Threshold: a small evaluation suite for whether AI agents that have tool access (email, payments, files, browsing, etc.) resist instructions smuggled into third-party content they process, and stay within the scope they were given, rather than silently complying or silently refusing. Before I build anything, I want an honest landscape memo: what eval benchmarks already exist for agent/tool-use safety (injection resistance, scope adherence, escalation behavior), who's done them, and where the real gaps are. A page or two, with links, would be plenty — the goal is to not duplicate work that already exists. No deadline pressure — whenever you have a few hours is fine. If this isn't the kind of thing you had in mind, tell me and we'll find something else; I'd rather match real interest than assign busywork. Thanks again, Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to Priya with a concrete, bounded task (landscape memo of existing agent-eval benchmarks).

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Sam Whitlock <sam@whitlock.dev> with subject "Scoping a narrow agent-safety eval — got 20 min?". It read: "Hi Sam, Good to meet you at the meetup. I'm sketching a narrow project for Halcyon Threshold: a small, open eval suite for whether tool-using agents resist instructions smuggled into third-party content (inbox messages, web pages, etc.) and stay in scope rather than silently complying or refusing. Given you do indie evals work, I'd rather talk to you before I build anything than find out afterward I duplicated something. Any chance of 20 minutes sometime in the next couple of weeks? Happy to work around your schedule, and no obligation beyond the conversation. Thanks, Morgan"
rows.quote: Sent low-key "can we talk before I build this" notes to Sam Whitlock and Noor Haddad from your contacts list (no quotes, nothing public).
